[[Beijing Guoan F.C.|Beijing Guoan]] won their first ever Chinese Super League title. The events during the [[2008 in Chinese football|2008 season]] saw [[Liaoning F.C.|Liaoning Hongyun]] relegated and [[Wuhan Optics Valley F.C.|Wuhan Optics Valley]] withdrawn. They were replaced by the promoted teams [[Jiangsu F.C.|Jiangsu Sainty]] and [[Chongqing Liangjiang Athletic F.C.|Chongqing Lifan]]. Zhejiang Greentown which is located in [[Hangzhou]], [[Zhejiang]] were renamed to [[Zhejiang Professional F.C.|Hangzhou Greentown]]. Each team is allowed to register a maximum of five foreign players and field four of them in starting line-up this season, one of whom must be from an [[Asian Football Confederation|AFC]] country.{{cite news| url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/blog/2009/mar/17/asian-champions-league-reorganisation | work=The Guardian | location=London | title=AFC lays down the law as it grasps for Uefa's coat-tails | first=John | last=Duerden | date=2009-03-17 | access-date=2010-04-23}} The league title sponsor is Italian tire manufacturer [[Pirelli]]. A three-year deal was announced on March 20, 2009.{{Cite web |url=http://www.iht.com/articles/ap/2009/03/20/sports/SOC-China-New-Sponsor.php |title=Archived copy |access-date=2009-03-20 |archive-date=2020-01-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200128092214/http://www.iht.com/articles/ap/2009/03/20/sports/SOC-China-New-Sponsor.php |url-status=dead }} [[Nike, Inc.|Nike]] have renewed sponsorship deal with Super League before season starts.
